newsitem.title: GERMANY: MG to buy BHF stake in AGIV.
newsitem.headline: MG to buy BHF stake in AGIV.

text.p: Metallgesellschaft AG (MG) plans to buy a 49.99 percent stake in industrial holding company AGIV AG from BHF-Bank AG, MG and BHF said on Monday.
The transaction has yet to be approved by their supervisory boards and by cartel authorities and still depended on the outcome of a due diligence examination, MG and BHF said in separate statements.
The price to be paid for the stake was not disclosed.
MG, a diversified industrial group, and BHF said they had reached agreement on the sale.
MG said the purchase will enable it to supplement its portfolio of market-leading companies and create a new division in process control and measurement technology.
"Existing MG activities in plant construction and construction technology could be rounded off or expanded," MG said. It added it would release further details later on Monday.
BHF-Bank said the sale marked an important step in the streamlining of its portfolio of industrial investments.
Loss-making AGIV omitted its dividend payment for last year, hitting BHF's net interest income which fell about two percent in the first six months of 1996.

AGIV, whose full name is AGIV Aktiengesellschaft fuer Industrie und Verkehrswesen, has said it made an operating loss of about 40 million marks in 1996 but has predicted a turnaround in 1997 through the sale of activities in a restructuring.

The company, whose businesses comprise mechanical engineering, electronics, electrical engineering, power supply, construction and transport, expects its annual sales to fall to about 6.5 billion marks by the end of the restructuring in 1998 from about 9.6 billion marks now.

AGIV aims to concentrate its activities on engineering, electronics and technical services. It said at the end of 1996 that it was selling its 74 percent stake in building group Wayss & Freytag to Dutch-based Hollandsche Beton Groep NV.
